keyVerseText: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
rootMeaning: The name יֵהוּא (Yêhûwʼ) derives from a contraction of the divine name יְהֹוָה (Yᵉhôvâh, Jehovah) combined with the pronoun הוּא (he), meaning 'Jehovah is He.' This etymology highlights a direct connection to God Himself, emphasizing the identity of the bearer as one who belongs to or represents Jehovah. Unlike a simple personal name, יֵהוּא carries the weight of divine association, signifying that the individual is defined in relation to the LORD.
usageInScripture: The word יֵהוּא appears 58 times in Scripture, primarily as a proper name for five different Israelites, most notably the king of Israel who ended the Omri dynasty. The top translations consistently render it as 'Jehu' or phrases including his name, such as 'And Jehu' or 'of Jehu,' indicating its use as a personal identifier rather than a title or descriptive term. This consistency shows the name's role as a marker of key historical figures, particularly in the northern kingdom of Israel, reflecting its importance in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יֵהוּא as 'Jehovah is He' enriches our grasp of biblical names as theological statements, not mere labels. The name's divine root reminds believers that God's sovereignty and identity are central even in the lives of His chosen leaders. Jehu, as a king and prophet, embodies God's authority and judgment, reinforcing the truth that God works through human agents to fulfill His purposes. This connection encourages faith in God's active presence and control over history, affirming His unchanging nature as the LORD.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 16:1, 'Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,' the name Jehu identifies the prophetic messenger through whom God communicates His judgment. The divine meaning embedded in Jehu's name underscores that this message is not merely human opinion but originates from Jehovah Himself. This highlights the authority behind the prophecy and assures readers that God's word is delivered through appointed individuals, reinforcing trust in His sovereign will.
